eComment - Community members can now comment on City Council agenda items online. The City has launched a new tool for public comment on City Council agenda items. The new tool, eComment, allows community members to conveniently submit comments on City Council agenda items, even if they are unable to attend the Council meeting to comment in person. When the City Council meeting agenda is posted online, an eComment link is placed next to the current agenda link on the Council Agenda page. The eComment period opens when the City Council agenda is posted and closes at noon the day of the meeting. Before the Council meeting, community members not only have the opportunity to read the staff reports and supporting materials, they can click on the eComment link and submit their position (support, oppose, or neutral) and comments on any or all of the agenda items. Once the public comment period closes, a report of all eComments will be provided to each Council member. By City Council direction, the initial trial of eComment will be for a one-year. Based on results from this trial, Council will determine whether to continue with the service and/or expand it to be used by Commissions.

Notice to the Public:
To ensure that the City meets your needs when addressing the City Council, all presentation materials which require the use of visual equipment need to be submitted to the City's IT Division at least 24 hours in advance of the meeting (except for appeal hearings where materials must be submitted 7 days in advance). This includes photographs, Microsoft Office documents (PowerPoint, Word, Excel). No CD's, DVD's, or USB thumb/flash drives will be accepted at the meeting. All materials must be in PC format and digital presentation items must be emailed to it-service-desk@encinitasca.gov . Please label all materials with the corresponding agenda item number. Should technical assistance be necessary, it will be available to presenters from 5:30 p.m. to 5:50 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Presentation of video/digital/photographs are considered part of the maximum time limit provided to speakers.
